nominees.name: Juan Ignacio Cirac

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum information
motivation: In 1995 Cirac and Zoller showed how laser-cooled ions in a trap can serve as a scalable quantum computer, giving the first concrete physical blueprint for universal quantum logic. Together with Jaksch and others they then proposed that atoms in optical lattices realize Hubbard models, founding analog quantum simulation. Their theory has been verified decisively in experiments: the superfluid-Mott insulator transition, quantum gas microscopy, and programmable atom arrays. Rainer Blatt turned the Cirac-Zoller scheme into reality, with the first CNOT gate on two ions, deterministic teleportation, multi-qubit entanglement and digital quantum simulation. Each step moved from conceptual proposal to precise experimental test. The work created quantum information science with atoms and ions as a discipline, complementing the 2012 and 2025 prizes. Today it underpins quantum computers, quantum simulators and quantum metrology worldwide.
